consensus_findings.description: Critical: PATCH /issues/{issue_id}/labels is an ordinary issue-update surface (Kanban drag-to-Ready) that calls IssueService.update but never maps ProjectionIssueMutationError to HTTP 403. create/update/close handlers do (`coordination_api.py:1355-1356,1446-1447,1478-1479`), yet patch_issue_labels (`coordination_api.py:3239-3289`) lets reserved-label attachment and registry-owned mutation refusals propagate uncaught. Deterministic probe: uncaught ProjectionIssueMutationError becomes HTTP 500 while the row remains unchanged, violating the OpenSpec SHALL that the issue API return HTTP 403 for those refusals.

Nit: mutate_issue_if_unowned always lists labels in the UPDATE SET clause (`039_projection_integrity_and_insert_events.sql:449-451`), so PostgreSQL fires UPDATE OF labels even when the patch omits labels. For a pre-039 unowned reserved-labelled row (not registry-owned, so the early ownership check passes), any ordinary status/title/close patch then hits enforce_projection_label_ownership and raises SQLSTATE 42501 reserved_projection_label instead of a structured JSONB reason. Integrity holds via rollback; the HTTP/MCP envelope becomes an exception string rather than projection_issue_immutable/reserved_projection_label.

Ordinary issue create/update cannot attach the reserved projection:autopilot-phase marker. IssueService.create and IssueService.update call _reject_reserved_projection_label which raises ProjectionIssueMutationError mapped to HTTP 403 in coordination_api.py. Database trigger enforce_projection_label_ownership (migration 039, lines 398-417) rejects any INSERT/UPDATE supplying the marker before work_queue_projection_ownership registration. Verified by live test test_database_rejects_unowned_spoofed_projection_issue and HTTP test test_ordinary_issue_api_cannot_cross_projection_boundary[create].

Ordinary issue update/close cannot mutate a registry-owned projection row. mutate_issue_if_unowned RPC (migration 039, lines 419-463) takes a row lock (FOR UPDATE), checks work_queue_projection_ownership before applying any allowlisted patch, and returns projection_issue_immutable which the HTTP layer maps to 403 (coordination_api.py:1445-1446, 1477-1478). Verified by live tests test_owned_same_generation_request_reactivates_terminal_canonical_issue and HTTP test test_ordinary_issue_api_cannot_cross_projection_boundary[update/close]. The row-locking RPC closes check/write races for all patched fields and batched closes.

Migration 039 projection RPCs insert an unlabelled row, register its UUID in work_queue_projection_ownership, then apply the exact canonical label pair transactionally. submit_task and reconcile_work_projection insert with labels=ARRAY[]::TEXT[], then INSERT INTO work_queue_projection_ownership(task_id) VALUES(v_id) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, then UPDATE work_queue SET labels=p_projection_labels WHERE id=v_id (migration 039, lines 151-194, 296-374). The enforce_projection_label_ownership trigger rejects post-migration unowned inserts/label updates (lines 398-417). First-insert SSE works via notify_projection_insert trigger on the labelled UPDATE (lines 465-496). Replay, concurrent generation serialization, and explicit administrator adoption of pre-039 rows all verified by live tests test_same_generation_submit_replay_clears_noncanonical_owned_labels, test_owned_projection_cannot_take_over_unowned_issue_key, test_039_upgrade_fails_closed_until_owner_registers_verified_row.

Keyed submit and reconcile authorize publish_work_projection in the service layer with the exact change resource and mode/change audit context. WorkQueueService.submit and reconcile_projection call get_policy_engine().check_operation with operation="publish_work_projection", resource=key.change_id, and context={"mode": "submit|reconcile", "change_id": key.change_id} (work_queue.py:777-798, 922-933). HTTP layer coordination_api.py:1204-1268 does the same before delegating to the service. Direct MCP/service callers cannot fall back to ordinary submit_work because the service layer itself selects the elevated operation when projection_key is present. Verified by test test_standard_trust_cannot_publish_projection returning HTTP 403.

Cedar policy mode resolves omitted trust through the same shared fail-closed resolver as native policy. CedarPolicyEngine._do_check_operation calls resolve_trust_level and on TrustResolutionError returns a deny decision without reaching mutation (policy_engine.py:732-753). Native policy does the same (policy_engine.py:195-206). Both engines deny before any mutating RPC. Verified by test test_admin_resolves_trust_when_context_omits_it and trust-resolution fail-open test test_reconcile_propagates_instead_of_writing_unscanned.

In-process converge() resolves the vendor panel using the reviewed worktree_path with explicit/local/coordinator/global precedence and retains SDK-only coordinator rosters. convergence_loop.py:610-616 calls _orchestrator_for_dispatch(None, worktree_path) when orchestrator and agents_yaml_path are omitted, matching the fixed CLI dispatcher resolution chain. Regression test test_converge_resolves_vendor_panel_from_reviewed_worktree fails if the stale coordinator-first constructor is used.

Labelled and legacy unlabelled modes are isolated in both directions before head or row mutation. Unlabelled requests against any registry-owned row return projection_mode_mismatch before mutation (submit_task lines 97-112, reconcile_work_projection lines 225-240). Labelled requests against any complete unowned keyed row return projection_key_collision (submit_task lines 97-112, reconcile_work_projection lines 225-240). Verified by live tests test_unlabelled_projection_cannot_mutate_owned_labelled_namespace[submit/reconcile] and test_labelled_projection_cannot_enter_unlabelled_keyed_namespace[submit/reconcile]. Exact-key replay, newer-generation reconcile, pre-039 upgrade, ordinary legacy cancellation, and head preservation all validated.

Direct MCP and HTTP-proxy submit/reconcile accept and forward the exact projection_labels pair. MCP tools submit_work and reconcile_work_projection accept projection_labels parameter and pass it to service layer (coordination_mcp.py:398-423). HTTP proxy proxy_submit_work and proxy_reconcile_work_projection forward projection_labels in request body (http_proxy.py:473-525). Every projection conflict returns structured HTTP 409 via _ProjectionProblemError mapping (coordination_api.py:115-135, 854-865) rather than a trigger exception. Verified by test test_proxy_submit_and_reconcile_projection_payloads and live PostgreSQL test suite.

Pre-registry N-to-N+1 fail-close is enforced. Both labelled SQL paths acquire pg_advisory_xact_lock then scan for associated unowned projection:autopilot-phase rows by payload change_id or exact change:<id> label, returning projection_key_collision before head or row mutation (migration 039, lines 97-112, 225-240). Live test test_039_upgrade_fails_closed_until_owner_registers_verified_row proves migration-038 generation N blocks N+1 repair with head remaining (INIT,0) until explicit work_queue_projection_ownership registration.

Projection-head/ownership invariants hold. work_queue_projection_heads is updated atomically within the per-change advisory transaction. work_queue_projection_ownership is the sole ownership authority; mutable payload fields and labels cannot confer ownership. Active canonical rows preserve lifecycle state; owned terminal rows are reactivated to pending with lifecycle fields cleared and emit projection refresh event (migration 039, lines 156-175, 305-320). Verified by live tests test_owned_same_generation_replay_preserves_nonterminal_status, test_owned_same_generation_request_reactivates_terminal_canonical_issue, test_terminal_reactivation_refreshes_connected_sse.

Canonical CLI persistence and ESCALATE resume work correctly. runner.py init, transition, escalate, apply-outcome, record-state-only-archetype, and project-state commands persist state before projection (design D8). enter_escalate increments total_iterations exactly once. Console-approved escalate_resume applies the canonical resolved edge before host projection. Resume reconciliation runs before gates/work. Verified by autopilot test suites: test_apply_outcome_contract.py (40 tests), test_runner_cli.py (15 tests), test_console_interviewer.py (10 tests).

Connected-client visibility via SSE works for first-insert, reconciliation, and terminal reactivation. Migration 037 emits label-update events; migration 039 emits first-insert event via notify_projection_insert trigger. event_stream.py converts both to SSE snapshot replacement. Verified by live tests test_connected_sse_refreshes_after_atomic_projection_reconciliation, test_connected_sse_refreshes_for_first_canonical_projection_insert, test_terminal_reactivation_refreshes_connected_sse — all complete within 1 second.

Coordinator-free isolation is preserved. QueueProjectionAdapter is constructed only for coordinated hosts; runner.py project-state imports it lazily. Local-parallel and sequential tiers perform zero projection-module imports/construction and zero projection submit/reconcile/label-helper calls. Isolation test test_phase_projection_isolation.py fails closed if try_submit_work, try_reconcile_work_projection, or coordinator-only label helpers are imported or called from free tiers. Pre-existing coordinator detection/archetype resolution imports are retained per D10.

none: Ordinary issue mutation is fail-closed at both boundaries. The database RPC locks the issue row before checking registry ownership, rejects the reserved marker, and applies every exposed update/close field in the same statement; the HTTP create, update, and close handlers map ProjectionIssueMutationError to 403.

none: All projection state conflicts—stale_projection, projection_generation_mismatch, projection_mode_mismatch, reconciliation_required, and projection_key_collision—are classified as structured HTTP 409 Problems. Invalid requests and policy denials remain separately mapped to 422 and 403, so the recovered SQL preflights do not leak ownership-trigger exceptions through projection endpoints.

none: In-process convergence uses the shared reviewed-checkout resolver with worktree_path whenever no explicit roster or injected orchestrator is supplied. The resolver implements explicit, reviewed-checkout-local, coordinator, then global-disk precedence and retains a coordinator roster when either CLI or SDK adapters are present.

none: The in-process host persists before every projection, reconciles loaded durable state before gates or phase work, projects all ordinary and ESCALATE transitions after saving, and never feeds queue responses into LoopState. Projection exceptions and non-success envelopes are bounded degradation results rather than state rollback.

none: Live PostgreSQL regressions cover both submit and reconcile mode isolation, exact head preservation, non-issue and unowned-issue key collisions, reserved-label spoof rejection, and owned terminal-row recovery. Fresh-migration upgrade coverage separately proves fail-closed pre-039 behavior followed by explicit administrator adoption.

none: Exact commit inspection confirms HEAD 34f3e5c74d88fd2d252b4a760c876cb8bc3fe91e differs from the validated implementation-and-architecture commit 96133ffe07592f6415406644b7587df715cd2e16 only by the validation ledger update, which records the round-13 recovery and pins 96133ffe as the validated source.

none: Earlier recovery seams hold under re-audit: pre-registry N-to-N+1 fail-close before head mutation; projection-head/ownership invariants with database-owned UUIDs only; canonical CLI persistence and ESCALATE resume (runner project-state after persist; enter_escalate increments total_iterations once); connected-client SSE refresh on label apply/reconcile/reactivation; coordinator-free isolation (QueueProjectionAdapter only for coordinated hosts; test_phase_projection_isolation.py passed).

FYI: Local MCP issue create/update/close still surface ProjectionIssueMutationError through the generic Exception envelope as success:false with an exception string (`coordination_mcp.py` issue handlers), whereas HTTP create/update/close return 403. The row is unchanged; only the failure envelope differs. Round-13 disposition accepted this as informational.

FYI: trg_work_queue_projection_insert_notify / notify_projection_insert (`039_...sql:465-496`) cannot observe reserved labels on the labelled RPC path because inserts are intentionally unlabelled; first-insert board/SSE refresh depends on migration 037's AFTER UPDATE notify when labels are applied. Behavior is correct; prior positive text that credited the INSERT trigger for first-insert SSE is inaccurate.
